newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: 300 Khmer Rouge fighters join Cambodian army.
newsitem.headline: 300 Khmer Rouge fighters join Cambodian army.

text.p: About 300 Khmer Rouge guerrillas were formally inducted into the royal Cambodian armed forces on Sunday in the west of the country.
Co-Defence Minister Tea Banh presided over the ceremony at which the defectors from the bellicose Maoist faction were each given food, medicine and two sets of army uniforms.

Major General Hul Savaon, regional commander for west and northwest Cambodia, said they came from eight rebel divisions based in Pursat and Battambang provinces and had broken with hardliners loyal to Pol Pot to join the government side.
Officials said they were a separate case from up to 4,000 guerrillas loyal to Ieng Sary, who broke with Khmer Rouge hardliners in August and agreed a ceasefire with the government.

King Norodom Sihanouk has granted an amnesty to Ieng Sary from a 1979 death sentence for his role in the genocide of more than one million Cambodians when he was foreign minister during Khmer Rouge rule.
First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh met Ieng Sary in rebel territory on Friday in the highest-level talks between the two sides to discuss a merger of forces.

Analysts said the unconditional defection of the 300 Khmer Rouge fighters could put pressure on Ieng Sary to drop demands for top central command posts and semi-autonomy and speed up a merger and access to his zones.

The guerrillas wore their olive green Khmer Rouge uniforms at the start of the ceremony and later changed into their new government uniforms. "We need medicine and food immediately not (top military) positions," said one commander, Charp Mao.
The Khmer Rouge signed a U.N.-brokered peace pact in 1991 but reneged on the deal and has been fighting the coalition government since elections in 1993.
